summary: Paige Bailey, engine lead for the DevRel team at Google DeepMind, presents on behalf of the generative media team (crediting Tom Hume, Demetri Horn, and others) covering three models: Veo 3 (video with native audio), Imagen 4 (static images), and Lyria 2 (music generation). The talk recaps Veo 2's creative control features released approximately one month prior: reference-powered videos, outpainting (including a Sphere/Wizard of Oz project), object addition/removal, character control with lip-syncing, style matching, camera controls via natural language, and first-to-last frame interpolation. Veo 2 benchmarks favorably against Runway Gen 4 and Kling in side-by-side human evaluations. Veo 3 represents a significant leap by natively composing audio and video tokens together—audio is integrated into the model itself, not a separate tool. It generates synchronized dialogue, sound effects, and background sounds with improved prompt adherence, stylistic consistency, and contextual consistency. Veo 3 also introduces a prompt writing feature that expands simple sentences into richer prompts the model better understands. Built on years of research including GQN and Walt, Veo 3 includes visible and SynthID watermarks. A French-language demonstration from the Paris team showcases dialogue and humor, including a skit about AGI. Access to Veo 3 is available via Google AI Ultra plan (many countries including the UK), Gemini mobile app for Pro subscribers (limited uses), and Vertex AI private preview, with V2 also available via Vertex AI for Gemini APIs. A code sample shows integration requires just a few lines specifying output bucket, input image, and aspect ratios. A Chick-fil-A commercial replication dramatically illustrates the workflow difference: Veo 2 required Gemini to segment the original video into prompts (due to an 8-second limitation), separate music generation, and manual stitching in Camtasia, while Veo 3 produced a comparable narrated result from a single prompt. The talk also covers Imagen 4's realism and typography (with Ross Lovegrove collaboration) and Lyria 2's music tools (Music AI Sandbox, MusicFX) with artist collaborations including Jacob Collier and Toro y Moi. Google is committed to expanding access and adding durability controls.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Model Overview
sections.summary: Paige Bailey introduces herself as engine lead for Google DeepMind's DevRel team, presenting on behalf of the generative media team. She outlines three models: Veo 3 (video and audio), Imagen 4 (static images), and Lyria 2 (music). She references Andrej Karpathy on video as a communication and education surface.

sections.title: Veo 2 Capabilities Recap
sections.summary: Recap of Veo 2 creative control features released approximately one month prior: reference-powered videos, outpainting (including Sphere/Wizard of Oz project), object addition/removal, character control with lip-syncing, style matching, camera controls via natural language, and first-to-last frame interpolation. Veo 2 benchmarks favorably against Runway Gen 4 and Kling in human rater comparisons.

sections.title: Veo 3 Introduction and Demonstrations
sections.summary: Veo 3 natively composes audio and video tokens together rather than pulling audio in as a tool. Demonstrations show synchronized audio including dialogue, music, and subtle background sounds. Key improvements over Veo 2 include prompt adherence, stylistic consistency, and contextual consistency. Built on years of research (GQN, Walt) with visible and SynthID watermarks. Artist partnerships include Darren Aronofsky.

sections.title: Imagen 4 and Lyria 2
sections.summary: Imagen 4 generates realistic images preserving detail across humans, animals, diverse styles, and typography, with artist collaborations including Ross Lovegrove. Lyria 2 offers high-fidelity music with granular creative controls through Music AI Sandbox and MusicFX. Real-time collaborations include Jacob Collier and Toro y Moi. Both incorporate SynthID watermarking.

sections.title: Text-to-Video Evolution and Image-to-Video
sections.summary: Demonstration of text-to-video evolution using a consistent raccoon-dancing-at-pyramids prompt: choppy 2023 Walt, LTX video (2024), Kling 2.0 (2025), Veo 2 (2024), and finally Veo 3. Image-to-video capabilities shown transforming a static image of a woman and puppy into dynamic video content.

sections.title: Veo 3 Prompt Writing and Audio Demonstrations
sections.summary: Continued demonstrations of stylized image-to-video transformations steered via natural language. Veo 3 introduces a prompt writing feature that expands simple sentences (e.g., raccoon at pyramids) into richer, more structured prompts the model better understands. A French-language Veo 3 video from the Paris team showcases dialogue, music, and humor, including a comedic skit about AGI. The detail level is noted as remarkable, with visible reflections in characters' eyes.

sections.title: Accessing Veo 3 and Code Sample
sections.summary: Veo 3 is accessible via Google AI Ultra plan (many countries including UK), Gemini mobile app for Pro subscribers (limited uses), and Vertex AI private preview. V2 is available via Vertex AI for Gemini APIs. An early access form is available via QR code. A code sample demonstrates integration requiring just a few lines specifying output bucket, input image, aspect ratios, and model selection.

sections.title: Chick-fil-A Commercial Replication: Veo 2 vs Veo 3
sections.summary: A Chick-fil-A commercial replication dramatically illustrates the workflow difference between Veo 2 and Veo 3. The Veo 2 process required giving Gemini the original video to create a detailed plan, segmenting into prompts due to an 8-second limitation, using separate music generation tools, and manual stitching in Camtasia with transitions. The Veo 3 process required only generating a description and submitting a single prompt, producing a comparable narrated result. Takeaways: Veo 3 is 'pretty magical,' Google is committed to expanding access and adding durability controls. The closing shows a static photo of Paige animated by Veo 3.
